units.source_excerpt: Designing the Optimal Snowboard Half-Pipe
units.function: Name the design object and optimization class directly.
units.reusable_pattern: Designing the Optimal {system}
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a design optimal without a defined objective and constraints.

units.source_excerpt: The two variables most correlated with judged performance are total vertical air and average degree of rotation.
units.function: Move from judged performance to two measurable design objectives.
units.reusable_pattern: Use {evidence} to nominate {metric_1} and {metric_2} as separate design objectives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat correlation as a causal scoring model.

units.source_excerpt: Vertical air is defined as maximum vertical distance above the coping, while rotation is measured by average degree of rotation.
units.function: Operationalize both performance branches before modeling.
units.reusable_pattern: Define {objective_1} relative to {reference}; define {objective_2} by {measurement}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not change metric semantics later.

units.source_excerpt: We first maximize vertical air and then investigate rotation, before discussing the tradeoff required for a practical course.
units.function: Map the reader through the two model branches and decision closure.
units.reusable_pattern: First solve {branch_1}; then solve {branch_2}; finally compare them under {decision constraints}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise a quantitative tradeoff if the body only gives qualitative extremes.

units.source_excerpt: A half-pipe contains a flat, transitions, vertical walls, and copings; current super-pipes vary in width, wall height, length, and slope.
units.function: Decompose the engineering object and its design dimensions.
units.reusable_pattern: Decompose {system} into {components}; define design space by {dimensions} and current ranges.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not optimize an undefined geometry.

units.source_excerpt: The paper compares approximate length, gradient, width, and wall height for the Nagano, Salt Lake, Torino, and Vancouver Olympic courses.
units.function: Use historical designs as an engineering baseline rather than validation.
units.reusable_pattern: Compare {n} existing designs on {aligned dimensions}; use ranges to bound candidates, not prove performance.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not infer optimality from historical adoption.

units.source_excerpt: The cross-section must be symmetric, continuous, inward-concave, and nearly vertical at the copings.
units.function: State the main geometric feasibility contract.
units.reusable_pattern: Require {symmetry}, {smoothness}, {curvature sign}, and {endpoint orientation} before optimization.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not accept a limiting curve that violates these conditions.

units.source_excerpt: The snowboarder and board are treated as a rigid inelastic point mass with one constant Coulomb friction coefficient.
units.function: Declare the mechanical abstraction and dissipation model.
units.reusable_pattern: Model {athlete-equipment} as {abstraction} with dissipation {law}; list excluded active and distributed mechanisms.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not apply dry-friction area independence to aerodynamic drag.

units.source_excerpt: The course slope is separated from the two-dimensional cross-section so vertical air is measured relative to the coping.
units.function: Set the coordinate and scope boundary for cross-section optimization.
units.reusable_pattern: Optimize {cross-section} at fixed {slope}; define response relative to {reference} and state omitted coupling.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim no loss of generality without a bound.

units.source_excerpt: With equal coping height, fixed initial kinetic energy, and no friction, the vertical air achieved is independent of cross-section shape.
units.function: Establish a conservative baseline and shape-independence result.
units.reusable_pattern: Under {conservative conditions}, {exit quantity} depends only on {initial energy and endpoint height}, not {path shape}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not carry path independence into dissipative models.

units.source_excerpt: Because shape does not change frictionless vertical air, the paper introduces minimum coping-to-coping travel time as a spectator-oriented secondary objective.
units.function: Signal an objective change and explain why it is introduced.
units.reusable_pattern: When {primary metric} is invariant, introduce {secondary metric} for {stakeholder reason}; keep its role distinct.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the secondary optimum a vertical-air optimum.

units.source_excerpt: The Euler-Lagrange first integral is transformed into cycloid parametric equations and interpreted with a rolling-circle construction.
units.function: Pair a variational derivation with a geometric interpretation.
units.reusable_pattern: Minimize {functional}, derive {first integral}, parameterize {solution}, and explain it through {geometric construction}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not suppress boundary compatibility.

units.source_excerpt: The paper defines tangent, normal, curvature, a force balance, Coulomb friction, and an energy balance along an arbitrary arc-length curve.
units.function: Build the dissipative model from geometry to forces to energy.
units.reusable_pattern: For curve {r(s)}, define {geometry}; derive {normal load}; set {friction law}; integrate in {energy balance}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not mix angle conventions.

units.source_excerpt: Semicircle, cycloid, and flat-oval families are parameterized before simulation so width, length, curvature, and exit speed can be compared.
units.function: Define candidate families and common outputs before results.
units.reusable_pattern: Define each candidate by {parameterization}, {domain}, and {constraints}; compute common {outputs}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not compare unmatched depths or lengths as pure shape effects.

units.source_excerpt: With a fixed rotation period, total rotations equal airtime divided by period; without pumping, airtime follows vertical projectile motion.
units.function: Reduce the rotation branch to an airtime objective under explicit conditions.
units.reusable_pattern: Under fixed {rotation period}, {rotation count}={airtime}/{period}; derive airtime from {trajectory model}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not exclude posture-dependent inertia without justification.

units.source_excerpt: At fixed width, the reported exit speeds are 15.7, 14.0, 16.5, and 16.0 m/s for the circle, cycloid, long oval, and short oval cases.
units.function: Report aligned candidate values under one control condition.
units.reusable_pattern: At fixed {control}, report {candidate:value} pairs with {secondary geometry outputs}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not compare candidates that change unreported dimensions.

units.source_excerpt: At fixed total arc length, the paper reports exit speeds and the resulting course widths for the same candidate families.
units.function: Repeat the comparison under a different controlled quantity.
units.reusable_pattern: Repeat {candidate comparison} at fixed {alternative control}; report induced changes in {other dimensions}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not combine conclusions from different control regimes silently.

units.source_excerpt: Across the plotted widths, the long flat oval ranks above the other tested families in the simulated exit response.
units.function: State the family ranking and tested domain.
units.reusable_pattern: Across {tested domain}, {candidate} ranks highest on {metric}; retain constraints and uncertainty.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not extrapolate to a degenerate boundary as a practical optimum.

units.source_excerpt: Dividing the exit-energy equation by one-half mass shows that exit speed is independent of rider mass under the chosen force law.
units.function: Use algebraic cancellation as an invariance check.
units.reusable_pattern: Cancel {factor} in {equation} to show {invariance}, conditional on {law assumptions}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not transfer invariance beyond the force law.

units.source_excerpt: The simulations use 0.01 m path steps and the paper states that a smaller-step rerun gave confidence in the results.
units.function: Expose discretization scale and the claimed convergence check.
units.reusable_pattern: Run at {step sizes}, report {output differences} and convergence rate before claiming stability.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call an unspecified rerun convergence.

units.source_excerpt: The paper varies the friction coefficient and plots the exit response for the long oval family.
units.function: Test the recommendation across a loss parameter range.
units.reusable_pattern: Vary {loss parameter} over {range}; stop trajectories at {physical event} and report recommendation reversals.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not plot negative kinetic energy as motion.

units.source_excerpt: The paper discusses air resistance, nonconstant friction, slope, snow surface, active athlete motion, and curvature limits as omitted mechanisms.
units.function: Inventory physical omissions after the result ranking.
units.reusable_pattern: After {result}, list omitted {mechanisms} and identify which outputs each could change.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not mislabel Coulomb curvature loss aerodynamic drag.

units.source_excerpt: The authors propose more conventional friction laws and three-dimensional extensions before turning to rotation.
units.function: Use limitations to motivate next models without claiming implementation.
units.reusable_pattern: Boundary {b} motivates extension {e}; label it proposed until equations, parameters, and results exist.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call proposed extensions model improvements already achieved.

units.source_excerpt: Vertical air and rotation prefer opposing geometric extremes, so no single cross-section maximizes both objectives.
units.function: State the objective conflict instead of a false universal optimum.
units.reusable_pattern: Objective {A} prefers {design region_A}, while {B} prefers {region_B}; therefore report a tradeoff set.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop before giving feasible conditional alternatives.

units.source_excerpt: A practical course requires balancing vertical air, rotation, safety, and buildability rather than choosing either limiting geometry.
units.function: Translate the conflict into a multi-constraint decision need.
units.reusable_pattern: Choose among {Pareto alternatives} using {safety}, {construction}, {cost}, and stakeholder preferences.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply the paper solved an absent Pareto model.

units.source_excerpt: The references combine engineering guidance, mechanics, calculus of variations, sports-performance, and general online sources.
units.function: Expose the source families supporting geometry, physics, and performance claims.
units.reusable_pattern: Group sources by {claim role} and cite each beside the borrowed equation, parameter, or fact.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use generic web pages when primary technical sources exist.

ambiguities: Optimal is a task label, not a validated claim.
